stories.title: Nvidia earnings, AI fan-fic, and the week in markets
stories.summary: Wall Street's AI worries are getting stranger. Chip company Nvidia reported record-breaking earnings on Wednesday, but tech investors are still panicking.

stories.title: Jesse Jackson lies in repose
stories.summary: The official memorials for Jesse Jackson began this week. The late civil rights leader is lying in repose at his Rainbow-Push Coalition headquarters in Chicago Thursday and Friday.

stories.title: Kyiv's elderly stay at home despite Russian attacks and power cuts
stories.summary: Older residents of Kyiv's many high-rises are learning to live with intermittent heat and electricity, cut off by Russian attacks.

stories.title: The mayor of Buffalo, N.Y., blames ICE for the death of nearly blind refugee
stories.summary: The mayor of Buffalo, New York, is blaming ICE for the death of a man who was released from their custody. The man was blind and did not speak English. He was found dead days after his release.

stories.title: As Trump dismantles asylum programs, Russians and Ukrainians fear for future
stories.summary: The Trump administration has been sending asylum seekers from Ukraine and Russia back to a warzone. One family in Minnesota says they fear for their lives.

stories.title: Bill Callahan's life was 'derailed' by having kids. Songwriting got him back on track
stories.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with the singer-songwriter Bill Callahan about his new album My Days of 58.
